identification.summary: RedGolf is Recorded Future's Insikt Group name for a threat activity group it assesses as highly likely Chinese state-sponsored, identified through a large cluster of new infrastructure tied to the custom Windows and Linux backdoor KEYPLUG [S1]. Insikt says RedGolf closely overlaps with activity reported publicly as APT41 and BARIUM [S1]. Insikt describes it as likely carrying out state-sponsored espionage in parallel with financially motivated operations for personal gain from at least 2014 onward [S1]. KEYPLUG use against US state governments was first publicly reported by Mandiant in March 2022 and attributed to APT41 [S2].
identification.firstObserved: Recorded Future: activity from at least 2014 for the overlapping APT41/BARIUM cluster [S1]. KEYPLUG intrusions reported by Mandiant from May 2021 to February 2022 [S2].
identification.notes: RedGolf is a Recorded Future cluster name, not a Microsoft name; no Microsoft mapping was confirmed in the sources gathered. Recorded Future states 'closely overlaps' with APT41/BARIUM, not that the clusters are identical [S1]. Press quoting an Insikt analyst says the groups are thought to be either the same or very closely affiliated [S5]. Facts about APT41 from Mandiant [S2] and the DOJ [S3][S4] describe that vendor/government cluster and are not asserted to be RedGolf-specific.

attribution.sponsor: People's Republic of China, per Recorded Future's assessment that RedGolf is highly likely a Chinese state-sponsored group [S1].
attribution.confidence: Recorded Future: highly likely Chinese state-sponsored [S1]. Some press coverage paraphrases this as 'likely' state-sponsored [S5]. China's Foreign Ministry denied the accusations, calling the report false information [S5][S7].
attribution.basis: Recorded Future infrastructure analysis of KEYPLUG command-and-control servers and tool overlap with APT41/BARIUM [S1][S5]. For the overlapping APT41 cluster, the US DOJ charged five Chinese nationals and two Malaysian nationals in September 2020, and prosecutors described the Chengdu 404 company as a front [S3][S4]. These are not indictments of RedGolf by name.

objectives: Espionage against government and other organizations, alongside financially motivated activity, per Recorded Future's description of the overlapping APT41/BARIUM cluster [S1]. Mandiant observed personally identifiable information exfiltration from US state government victims but said the campaign goals were unknown and it could not rule out financial motivation [S2].

sectors: Industrial sectors in Italy (KEYPLUG, Tinexta report)
regions: United States (state governments, per Mandiant on APT41/KEYPLUG) [S2]
United States government entities reportedly targeted by RedGolf [S5]
targeting.notes: Insikt listed the sectors above for RedGolf and did not name specific victims [S1][S5]. Insurance and telecommunications victims come from Mandiant's APT41 reporting [S2]. The Italian KEYPLUG case is attributed to APT41 by Tinexta Cyber, not to RedGolf [S6].

capabilities.summary: KEYPLUG is a custom modular backdoor written in C++ with Windows and Linux variants. It supports HTTP, TCP, KCP over UDP and WSS for command and control [S2]. Mandiant saw APT41 use it with Cloudflare-fronted WSS C2 and dead drop resolvers in forum posts, ViewState deserialization, a USAHerds zero-day (CVE-2021-44207), Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228), SQL injection, Cobalt Strike BEACON, BADPOTATO, Mimikatz and DNS-based exfiltration [S2]. Insikt additionally saw RedGolf infrastructure using Cobalt Strike, PlugX and dynamic DNS domains, which are common among Chinese state-sponsored groups [S5]. Tinexta reported a .NET loader that decrypts the KEYPLUG payload with AES in a 2024 Italian case [S6].

campaigns.name: DOJ charges against APT41-linked individuals
campaigns.summary: The DOJ announced charges against seven people (five Chinese nationals, two Malaysian nationals) over hacking of more than 100 companies, from three indictments dated August 2019 and August 2020. Prosecutors described Chengdu 404 as a front company. This concerns the overlapping APT41 cluster, reported here via Dark Reading and a search listing of the DOJ release.

campaigns.name: APT41 KEYPLUG campaign against US state governments
campaigns.summary: Mandiant reported at least six US state government networks compromised, with initial access via ViewState deserialization, the USAHerds zero-day and Log4Shell. KEYPLUG Windows was heavily used June to December 2021 and KEYPLUG.LINUX deployed after Log4Shell exploitation. Two earlier victims were re-compromised in February 2022.

campaigns.name: Insikt report on RedGolf KEYPLUG infrastructure
campaigns.summary: Insikt identified a large cluster of new KEYPLUG infrastructure and attributed it to RedGolf. The Hacker News reported the cluster as 42 C2 IP addresses tracked as GhostWolf, seen from at least 2021 to 2023, alongside Cobalt Strike, PlugX and dynamic DNS domains. China denied the findings.

campaigns.name: KEYPLUG implant against Italian industries
campaigns.summary: Tinexta Cyber's Zlab reported a previously undetected KEYPLUG implant used against several Italian industries over months and linked it to APT41. This is a vendor attribution to APT41, not RedGolf.

diamond.adversary: Highly likely Chinese state-sponsored cluster overlapping APT41/BARIUM, with espionage and financially motivated activity [S1].
diamond.capability: KEYPLUG Windows and Linux backdoor, Cobalt Strike, PlugX, and for the overlapping APT41 cluster web-application exploitation including a zero-day and Log4Shell [S2][S5].
diamond.infrastructure: Cluster of new KEYPLUG C2 servers (reported as 42 IPs, GhostWolf) and dynamic DNS domains [S1][S5]. APT41 used Cloudflare-fronted WSS C2 and forum dead drop resolvers [S2].
diamond.victim: Aviation, automotive, education, government, media, IT and religious organizations; US government entities reportedly [S1][S5]. APT41 victims include six US state governments [S2].
diamond.socioPolitical: State-aligned espionage coexisting with profit-seeking, consistent with the PRC contractor ecosystem described in the DOJ charges against APT41-linked individuals [S1][S3][S4].
diamond.technology: Internet-facing web applications with exposed or default ASP.NET machine keys, unpatched Java logging libraries (Log4j), and mixed Windows/Linux server estates [S2].

gaps: The Recorded Future report text could not be opened (host unreachable from this environment); RedGolf claims rely on search-result summaries and press coverage of the report [S1][S5][S7].
The DOJ press release was not opened; DOJ details come from a search listing and Dark Reading coverage [S3][S4].
Exact overlap between RedGolf and APT41/BARIUM is unresolved: Recorded Future says 'closely overlaps' [S1].
No Microsoft actor name mapping for RedGolf was found; a search suggested BARIUM and Brass Typhoon are Microsoft names for APT41 but no primary Microsoft mapping was opened.
No victims named by Insikt; the 42-IP GhostWolf figure comes from secondary coverage only [S5].
No MITRE ATT&CK group entry for RedGolf confirmed.
Whether the 2024 Italian KEYPLUG activity is RedGolf is unknown [S6].

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Internet-facing web applications (ASP.NET, Java) and Windows/Linux servers at government and contractor-adjacent organizations are key terrain [S2]. STEP 2: The adversary exploits new vulnerabilities within hours (Log4Shell) and reuses a static machine key across installations, so patch windows are short [S2]. STEP 3: Template is web-app exploitation, then KEYPLUG with Cloudflare-fronted WSS C2, Cobalt Strike and credential theft, then data exfiltration including over DNS [S2][S5]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued espionage and opportunistic access against government and industry using KEYPLUG [S1]. MDCOA is rapid mass exploitation of a newly disclosed web-app flaw against DoD-adjacent hosts, combined with financially motivated activity that could mask intent [S1][S2]. Candidate indicators: Linux files split as xaa-xad, modified existing SYSTEM scheduled tasks, DNS queries carrying hex-encoded subdomains, and WSS traffic to Cloudflare ranges with an unusual SNI/host [S2].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track KEYPLUG and dynamic DNS infrastructure feeds and fold vendor reporting into hunt priorities [S1][S5]. (2) Authorities: attribution is vendor-level (Recorded Future); do not treat it as government attribution when tasking or reporting [S1]. (3) Mission assurance: inventory internet-facing ASP.NET/Java applications and rotate default machine keys [S2]. (4) Coordination: share indicators with DC3 and partner networks; state and commercial victims in prior campaigns were in sectors adjacent to defense supply chains [S1][S2].

provenance.importedSummary: Recorded Future’s Insikt Group has identified a large cluster of new operational infrastructure associated with use of the custom Windows and Linux backdoor KEYPLUG. We attribute this activity to a threat activity group tracked as RedGolf, which is highly likely to be a Chinese state-sponsored group. RedGolf closely overlaps with threat activity reported in open sources under the aliases APT41/BARIUM and has likely carried out state-sponsored espionage activity in parallel with financially motivated operations for personal gain from at least 2014 onward.
